newsitem.title: FRANCE: Emmanuelli to head French parliament finance panel.
newsitem.headline: Emmanuelli to head French parliament finance panel.

text.p: Former Socialist Party leader Henri Emmanuelli was elected chairman of the National Assembly's finance commission on Tuesday, succeeding centrist parliamentarian Pierre Mehaignerie.
Socialist Didier Migaud was elected as rapporteur of the budget, a key post in steering finance legislation through parliament. He takes over from Philippe Auberger.

Emmanuelli, a 52-year-old former banker, chaired the influential finance commission between 1991 and 1992 and is a former budget minister but has since become tangled in controversy over party financing.
A French court gave him an 18-month suspended sentence last week for illicit party fund-raising activities.
The Lyon court said Emmanuelli, who was re-elected to the National Assembly in the June 1 election that returned the Socialists to office, had made no personal profit from the financing scheme.
It rejected a state prosecutor's plea to ban him from holding elected office for a year.
It sentenced two former Socialist parliamentarians to 18 months suspended, and cleared another former Socialist Party treasurer, Andre Laignel.
A former Socialist party treasurer in the 1980s and leader in 1994-95, Emmanuelli was charged with handling stolen goods and influence-peddling.

He had already been convicted on similar charges in a 1995 trial in Brittany when he was given a one-year suspended jail term and a 30,000 franc ($5,150) fine for receiving illicit campaign funds from a front company run by party insiders.

All mainstream French parties ran covert funding schemes before a 1990 law put party finances on a legal footing. Magistrates are investigating similar cases involving the centre-right RPR and UDF parties and the Communist party.
